summary: Arkwood Retail — routing fanout oscillation causing duplicate completions, streaming resets, and billing spike
description: Issue summary: On 2026-03-10 08:23 UTC Arkwood Retail observed a sudden increase in duplicate completions, transient streaming resets, and a correlated billing surge. Customer reported widespread user-facing timeouts in their chat feature and duplicate messages appearing in production.
impact: Multiple Arkwood endpoints (chat assist and order-intent classifiers) experienced duplicated completions and intermittent stream truncation for ~42 minutes. Estimated billable duplicate tokens: ~1.2M tokens. Severity impacted Arkwood's afternoon traffic window (high revenue period).
environment_details: Dedicated GPU pool (dedicated-arkwood-us-east), control plane region us-east-1, routing policy: tiered-fallback (dedicated -> hosted-lowcost). Autoscaler configured with burst pools enabled.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send concurrent streaming chat requests (~200 RPS) pinned to model redwood/roc-7b-v1 on dedicated-arkwood-us-east.
2) Observe responses: clients receive rapid duplicate completions (same conversation id, different completion ids) and occasional stream reset (HTTP/2 RST_STREAM).
3) Reproduce when routing policy detects short-lived capacity dip in dedicated pool and routes to hosted variant then back within seconds.
observed_behavior: Routing controller oscillated between dedicated and hosted variants on a per-request basis for a subset of customer traffic. The serving-runtime accepted duplicate inflight work (lack of idempotency enforcement across route changes). Retries + replays combined with streaming reconnects produced duplicate outputs and extra token billing.
initial_mitigation: 1) Support placed Arkwood traffic into a temporary static route pinned to dedicated-arkwood-us-east (bypassed tiered-fallback) at 08:29 UTC. 2) Rate-limited automated client retries at the edge for Arkwood (6-second backoff). 3) Eng disabled burst pooling for the dedicated pool to stabilize autoscaler behavior.
timeline: 2026-03-10 08:23 UTC - Arkwood alerts to support (duplicate messages & timeouts).
2026-03-10 08:25 UTC - Support triaged as P0 and paged routing/serving on-call. Slack thread #support-arkwood created.
2026-03-10 08:29 UTC - Temporary static pinning applied for Arkwood traffic; immediate drop in duplicates observed for pinned flows.
2026-03-10 09:05 UTC - Eng identified autoscaler health-check flapping (threshold too aggressive) leading to transient pool capacity flips.
2026-03-10 09:27 UTC - Hotfix deploy: increase health-check stabilizer and enable route-change debounce in routing controller (canary 10% then 100%).
2026-03-10 09:40 UTC - Full rollout complete. Monitoring shows normal completion rate; billing anomaly captured for reconciliation.
2026-03-10 10:00 UTC - Customer notified of resolution and temporary billing mitigation initiated.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Autoscaler health-check window too aggressive; small transient GC/latency spikes marked nodes unhealthy and triggered routing fallback.
Hypothesis B: Routing controller lacked debounce; immediate fallback to hosted variant created per-request route flips which allowed duplicate dispatch.

Finding: Correlated node-level OOM-kernel reclaim spikes on two gpus in dedicated-arkwood-us-east pool; health-check threshold (3s) considered nodes unhealthy and removed them briefly; routing controller reacted within 500ms and started routing to hosted variant. When nodes recovered, routing flipped back.
customer_communication_summary: 2026-03-10 08:31 UTC - Support: 'We see elevated duplicate completions and are applying a temporary pin to stabilize.'
2026-03-10 09:10 UTC - Support -> Arkwood CSM: 'We have a hotfix rolling, expect normal behavior in the next 15-30 minutes. We're investigating billing impact.'
2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - Support -> Arkwood: 'Issue resolved; initiating billing reconciliation and follow-up action items. Dedicated account team will share a credit estimate within 24 hours.'
resolution_notes: Root cause: aggressive autoscaler health-check + routing controller rapid fallback led to per-request route oscillation. Fixes applied: (1) increased health-check stabilization window from 3s to 12s for dedicated pools, (2) routing controller route-change debounce of 5s added to avoid per-request flips, (3) serving-runtime patched to enforce request-level idempotency keys for in-flight deduplication across route changes.
workaround_and_rollout: Temporary: pin Arkwood to dedicated pool while hotfix developed and rolled out.
Hotfix rollout: canary 10% at 09:27 UTC -> full roll at 09:40 UTC. Monitored for 30m; metrics stable.
Billing: provisional credit issued to Arkwood for estimated duplicate tokens; reconciliation engineering ticket opened for exact accounting.
postincident_action_items: ENG-1281: Harden autoscaler health-checks across all dedicated pools (owner: Priya Kumar) - due 2026-03-17.
ROUTING-402: Add route-change debounce and configurable threshold per customer tier (owner: Omar Reyes) - due 2026-03-15.
SERVE-777: Implement cross-route idempotency middleware in serving-runtime (owner: Dmitri Orlov) - due 2026-03-24.
SRE-900: Run capacity soak tests on dedicated-arkwood-us-east and verify no OOM reclaim during peak traffic (owner: Lina Park) - due 2026-03-16.
CS-250: Follow-up with Arkwood CSM to confirm billing credit and collect any customer tickets impacted (owner: Elena Morales) - due 2026-03-12.
billing_and_compensation: Initial provisional credit equal to estimated duplicate token usage (~1.2M tokens) applied to Arkwood account. Finance and billing engineering to validate and issue final credit by 2026-03-14. No contractual SLA penalty expected after remediation; Arkwood requested written summary and credit confirmation.
